thread:
sanjay: Heads up — during 13B onboarding in ap-southeast we saw p50 ~22ms but p99 jumped to ~1.8s under the same concurrency. Not obvious why. Can we sketch a capacity plan for a Dedicated pool to absorb this pattern?

jia: Ugh. Was that on H100 or A100? Kernel fallback or some long-kernel path?

sanjay: H100. We ran q4f16 and q8fx experiments. q4f16 improved median but p99 still spiked. Looking at logs it coincides with long seq completions and a big KV cache miss storm when many canaries hit new model simultaneously.

eva: Possible warmup issue + continuous batching mixing short and long requests. For Dedicated sizing I usually budget for two slices: low-latency slice (short requests) + long-tail slice (heavy seqs). That lets autoscaler scale the long-tail without hurting short path.

marc: Can you share the wrk style test you used? I want to reproduce locally.

sanjay: Sure — simple synthetic:

```
wrk -t12 -c200 -d120s --script=long_seq.lua https://dedicated.internal/model/13b
-- payloads: 32-token warmups + 1024-token spikes at 1 rps per connection
```

This pattern produces the p99 spike in ap-southeast but not in us-west.

jia: Interesting regional delta. Could be kernel selection differences (driver/kernel combo) or thermal throttling on that AZ. Can we run the same on a test H100 in eu-west? If p99 is lower there we know it's region-specific.

eva: Also try turning off continuous-batch merging for that experiment to isolate whether batching is amplifying KV miss storms.

ops-bot: Deploy event: canary of model-13b-qmix rolled to ap-southeast at 2078004220 by sanjay

marc: Quick numbers from my eu-west run: p50 18ms, p95 120ms, p99 480ms (q4f16). So still worse but not 1.8s.

sanjay: Thanks. So plan: for Dedicated capacity sizing I propose: base concurrency target = expected steady qps * 1.2 + 15 reserved for canaries; autoscale headroom = 40% for pools serving models with long-seq variance; reserve a hot-slice of ~2 GPUs per region to absorb KV warmups. Thoughts?

jia: 40% headroom sounds conservative but reasonable until we root-cause. Suggest we also add an automated circuit-breaker: if p99 > 1s for 30s, route new requests to fallback quantized variant (q8fx) and spawn extra nodes.

eva: Agree on circuit-breaker. Also track 'kv_cache_miss_rate' metric by model and region — if miss_rate > 5% for 1m, trigger pre-warm (run synthetic prefill on a subset of GPUs).

marc: For sizing calc: if single H100 does ~1200 tok/s median for 13B at our config, with target concurrency 200 steady we need ~2.5 GPUs (account for batching). So round up to 3 GPUs per pool for baseline, plus 40% headroom = +2 => 5 GPUs. Hot-slice of 2 GPUs makes 7. That aligns with our canary budget.

sanjay: Nice. Can someone capture this as a short runbook snippet? I'll need it for Dedicated sales sizing notes.

eva: I'll add a short runbook entry to the ops handbook later today. Quick bullet draft:
- baseline_per_pool = ceil((qps * avg_tokens_per_request / per_gpu_tok_s) / batching_efficiency)
- headroom_pct = 40% for long-tail models
- hot_slice = min(2, ceil(baseline_per_pool * 0.2))
- autoscale_policy: scale_up when p95 > target_p95 or kv_cache_miss_rate > 5% for 60s

jia: Also recommend a short kernel audit in ap-southeast infra team — different driver/firmware can change attention kernel selection and that matches the regional delta.

marc: FYI I created a quick chart and uploaded a PNG: https://internal.charts/redwood/13b-apac-headroom.png (shows p99 spike aligned with warmup bursts).

sanjay: Great. Next steps: 1) run controlled experiment with batching disabled (eva), 2) kernel audit request (jia), 3) add runbook bullets + circuit-breaker (eva + marc). I'll coordinate Dedicated sizing doc for sales. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Note: autoscale policy template "long-tail-heavy" created by marc at 2078004800

eva: Thanks — I'll post the runbook edit when done. If we still see 1.8s p99 after kernel parity, we escalate to model team for tokenization/decoder behavior.

sanjay: Thanks everyone — scheduling a 15min follow-up after experiments.
